best_for: People who already use a Yandex ID for mail and search and want a Chromium browser that syncs their passwords and cards through it.

points.title: Sync runs through a Yandex ID
points.text: Passwords, bank cards, bookmarks, open tabs, history, extensions and settings sync between devices once you sign in with the same Yandex ID. You can switch each type off. It does not sync with other browsers such as Chrome.

points.title: Chrome and Opera extensions
points.text: It installs extensions from the Chrome and Opera catalogs. Some named extensions are blocked as unsafe, and add-ons that replace the new tab page are ignored.

points.title: Built-ins you can only switch off
points.text: It ships with preinstalled add-ons such as an ad blocker and Yandex services. These cannot be removed, only disabled, and some older Yandex add-ons are no longer maintained.

points.title: Phishing warnings
points.text: Yandex says the browser checks sites for phishing and warns you before you open one. Saving bank cards requires setting a master password first.

points.title: Deleted means gone
points.text: Once you delete synced data from Yandex's servers it cannot be restored, so export anything you want to keep before wiping it.

points.title: Linux lags behind
points.text: The Linux build here is a Flathub package verified for Yandex, x64 only, and it is on 26.8 while Windows is on 26.11. Yandex also offers DEB and RPM packages on its own site.

points.title: Per-user Windows install
points.text: The Windows installer goes into your user profile, so no admin rights are needed. The Windows listing keeps 127 versions; macOS (Intel and Apple silicon, macOS 13 and later) and Linux list only the current release.
